Chapter 7: The Reluctant Follower – When Others Stay Behind
You know, not everyone’s ready to move forward at the same pace. As the little person in the story found new cheese and grew more confident, he kept thinking about his friend—still waiting, back in that old, familiar corner of the maze.
He left little notes behind, hoping they’d be discovered. But deep down, he understood something important: you just can’t force change on someone else. Everybody has to reach their own moment of readiness.
If you think about it, this happens all the time in real life—with our families, at work, or among friends. Maybe you’ve been there yourself. One friend in the group remembered trying to help a sibling who felt stuck in a job that just wasn’t bringing any joy anymore. She tried giving advice, shared her own experiences—even gently nudged her sibling toward something new. But nothing really changed, not until her sibling was ready to take that first step.
And you know, it’s tough to watch someone you care about stay stuck. The urge to jump in and fix things, to push someone forward—it’s so strong, isn’t it? But the story reminds us: everyone moves at their own pace. Sometimes, the best thing you can do is leave a bit of encouragement, and trust that when the time’s right, they’ll find their own way.
The friends talked about how much patience and compassion matter in these moments. Change is incredibly personal. What feels possible and exciting for one person might seem overwhelming to someone else. The maze we face is different for each of us—and so is the journey through it.
In the end, they realized that, while you can’t walk someone else’s path for them, you can always offer support, share your own story, and just be there when they’re ready to move. Because, ultimately, the decision to change has to come from within.
